### OBL-018 — Software bill of materials production

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | NTIA (SRC-031) |
| Authority type | official-guidance |
| Citation | NTIA minimum elements for an SBOM |
| Locator | https://www.ntia.gov/report/2021/minimum-elements-software-bill-materials-sbom |
| Source version | 2021 report |
| Verified on | 2026-08-19 |
| Jurisdiction | US-FEDERAL |
| Applicability | REFERENCE |
| Trigger | Federal software procurement, or a district or state procurement that asks for an SBOM. |
| Control family | SOFTWARE SUPPLY CHAIN |
| Control status | IMPLEMENTED |
| Evidence status | CURRENT |
| Owning route | WP-037, closed by DEC-017 |
| Review requirement | none recorded |
| Review trigger | Change of SBOM format or emitted version |

**What the source states.** NTIA defines minimum elements. The document is guidance and does not itself bind private parties.

**Obligation.** Defines the baseline SBOM data fields including author, timestamp, supplier, component name and version, and dependency relationships.

**SSLS interpretation.** The existing pipeline already satisfies the shape of this guidance for the current dependency set. That is a capability statement, not a compliance statement.

**Current phase.** Reference. SSLS produces an SBOM voluntarily through the WP-037 evidence pipeline.

**Future phase.** Becomes a procurement condition in federal sales and increasingly in state procurement.

**Required control.** Reproducible SBOM generation bound to a commit.

**Current control.** CycloneDX SBOM generated by the WP-037 pipeline and recorded as EV-SBOM with an artifact hash.

**Evidence required.** SBOM artifact bound to the producing commit. Minimum method: Automated pipeline evidence.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that it generates a CycloneDX SBOM per pipeline run.

**Claim refused.** SBOM compliant; NTIA conformant

**Note.** The emitted CycloneDX version must be stated because the ratified standard and latest spec differ. See CNF-002.

### OBL-019 — Dependency vulnerability identification and remediation

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | Center for Internet Security (SRC-025) |
| Authority type | voluntary-framework |
| Citation | CIS Controls v8.1, Control 7 |
| Locator | https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/v8-1 |
| Source version | 8.1 |
| Verified on | 2026-08-19 |
| Jurisdiction | NOT-JURISDICTIONAL |
| Applicability | APPLIES-NOW |
| Trigger | SSLS maintains a software product with third-party dependencies. |
| Control family | VULNERABILITY MANAGEMENT |
| Control status | IMPLEMENTED |
| Evidence status | CURRENT |
| Owning route | WP-037, closed by DEC-017 |
| Review requirement | none recorded |
| Review trigger | Each lockfile change |

**What the source states.** CIS publishes voluntary safeguards. Adoption is elective.

**Obligation.** Recommends continuous identification and remediation of vulnerabilities in software assets.

**SSLS interpretation.** SSLS treats this as an internal operating rule because it is cheap now and expensive to retrofit.

**Current phase.** Applies now as an adopted internal practice. It is not a legal duty.

**Future phase.** Becomes a procurement expectation in district and state security reviews.

**Required control.** Repeatable dependency advisory scan with recorded triage and remediation.

**Current control.** Pipeline advisory scan via the npm bulk advisory endpoint, with WP-037 triage, remediation and post-remediation rescan recorded as EV-021 to EV-025.

**Evidence required.** Scan artifact plus triage and remediation records. Minimum method: Automated scan with retained artifacts; single-source and point-in-time.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that a scan completed and matched no advisories in its recorded scope at a stated time.

**Claim refused.** No vulnerabilities; secure dependencies; independently validated

**Note.** bun audit remains unable to complete in the environment. That limitation is preserved in EV-VULN.

### OBL-020 — Dependency licence posture

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | Linux Foundation SPDX project (SRC-029) |
| Authority type | standard |
| Citation | SPDX 3.0.1 licence identifiers |
| Locator | https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0/ |
| Source version | 3.0.1 |
| Verified on | 2026-08-19 |
| Jurisdiction | INTERNATIONAL |
| Applicability | APPLIES-NOW |
| Trigger | SSLS distributes or hosts software containing third-party components. |
| Control family | SOFTWARE SUPPLY CHAIN |
| Control status | PARTIAL |
| Evidence status | CURRENT |
| Owning route | WP-037 for inventory; legal interpretation unassigned |
| Review requirement | LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED |
| Review trigger | First commercial distribution |

**What the source states.** SPDX defines identifiers and format. It does not state what any licence requires.

**Obligation.** Provides standard identifiers and a data model for communicating component licence information.

**SSLS interpretation.** Inventory is automatable; licence interpretation is not. The register separates the two.

**Current phase.** Applies now as an internal practice. Licence obligations themselves come from each component's licence, not from SPDX.

**Future phase.** Becomes a procurement and legal review input at first commercial distribution.

**Required control.** Automated licence inventory with a flag for components requiring legal review.

**Current control.** Pipeline licence inventory recorded as EV-LICENSE with a count of components requiring legal review.

**Evidence required.** Inventory artifact plus a reviewed determination for flagged components. Minimum method: Automated inventory; human review for interpretation.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that it inventories licences. It may not state that its licence posture is cleared.

**Claim refused.** Licence compliant; legally cleared

**Note.** PARTIAL because inventory exists and interpretation does not.

| Source | OpenSSF (SRC-030) |

| Verified on | 2026-08-19 |
| Jurisdiction | NOT-JURISDICTIONAL |
| Applicability | REFERENCE |
| Trigger | A customer or partner asks for build provenance attestation. |
| Control family | SOFTWARE SUPPLY CHAIN |
| Control status | PARTIAL |
| Evidence status | NOT-PRODUCED |
| Owning route | Unassigned |
| Review requirement | none recorded |
| Review trigger | First provenance request |

**What the source states.** OpenSSF publishes the framework. Levels are self-assessed unless independently verified.

**Obligation.** Defines graded build provenance and source integrity requirements.

**SSLS interpretation.** No SLSA level is claimed, and the existing commit binding is not equivalent to a provenance attestation.

**Current phase.** Reference. SSLS records commit-bound build evidence but produces no signed provenance attestation.

**Future phase.** May become a procurement expectation for hosted district software.

**Required control.** Signed build provenance if a level is ever claimed.

**Current control.** Commit-bound build and test evidence with input-set hashes. No attestation signing.

**Evidence required.** Signed provenance attestation. Minimum method: Automated attestation from a trusted builder.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** SLSA Level 3; provenance verified

**Note.** Source version date is UNVERIFIED.
